\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Generating Function: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Hermite.GeneratingFunction}.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Generating Function: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a Hermite exponential product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_hermite_mul_exp_quadratic}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_hermite_mul_exp_quadratic}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $k$ and complex numbers $x,z$, the function $w\mapsto
H_k(x-w)\exp(xw-w^2/2)$ has derivative at $w=z$ equal to $H_{k+1}(x-z)\exp(xz-z^2/2)$,
where $H_k$ denotes the $k$th Hermite polynomial.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivatives of the Hermite generating exponential]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.iteratedDeriv_exp_quadratic}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.iteratedDeriv_exp_quadratic}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_hermite_mul_exp_quadratic}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $k\ge 0$ and all complex numbers $x,z$, the $k$th complex derivative
at $z$ of $w\mapsto\exp(xw-w^2/2)$ equals $H_k(x-z)\exp(xz-z^2/2)$, where $H_k$ is the
Hermite polynomial.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Hermite generating function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_generating_function}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_generating_function}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.iteratedDeriv_exp_quadratic}
\difficulty{4}
For all real numbers $x$ and $t$, the Hermite polynomials satisfy
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} H_j(x)\frac{t^j}{j!}=\exp\!\left(tx-\frac{t^2}{2}\right),
\]
where $H_j$ is the degree-$j$ Hermite polynomial.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Normalized Hermite series term]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermite_generating_summand}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermite_generating_summand}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $j$ and real numbers $x,t$, the $j$th term formed from the
normalized Hermite polynomial satisfies
\[
H_j(x)\frac{t^j}{\sqrt{j!}}=\operatorname{He}_j(x)\frac{t^j}{j!},
\]
where $\operatorname{He}_j$ is the (unnormalized) Hermite polynomial of degree $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Generating function for normalized Hermite polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermite_generating_function}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermite_generating_function}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_generating_function, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermite_generating_summand}
\difficulty{1}
For all real numbers $x$ and $t$, the series with $j$th term $H_j(x)t^j/j!$, where $H_j$
is the normalized Hermite polynomial of degree $j$, converges to $\exp(tx-t^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}
